claim: UPI is an instant payment system developed by NPCI and built over IMPS infrastructure.
caveat: Do not depict physical money moving through a cable.

claim: NPCI operates/co-ordinates the UPI network and routes transaction messages between participants.
caveat: 'Switch/routing layer' is an accessible analogy; avoid overclaiming internal implementation.

claim: The remitter bank authenticates the UPI PIN and debits the sender's account in the common bank-linked flow.
caveat: Scope to a regular bank-account UPI payment.

claim: The beneficiary bank credits the receiving account.
caveat: Exact messaging and exception handling vary.

claim: A third-party UPI app is not the same thing as the underlying bank account or UPI network.
caveat: Some apps are bank apps; avoid implying identical corporate structures.

claim: UPI is designed to be available 24x7 to customers.
caveat: Outages and bank/network issues can still occur.

claim: Customer-facing payment confirmation and interbank settlement/reconciliation are distinct processes.
Pending or failed transactions can involve technical declines or delayed confirmation; universal instant refund promises are unsafe.
caveat: No fixed refund SLA in narration.

claim: UPI PIN authorizes the sender-side bank transaction and should never be shared.
caveat: Distinguish sending money from approving a collect request.

claim: A QR code or UPI ID helps identify the payment destination but does not prove the recipient is trustworthy.
caveat: Not a claim about QR cryptography.
